title: 2000 IMO Problem 1
statement:
Two circles \(G_1\) and \(G_2\) intersect at two points \(M\) and \(N\).
Let \(AB\) be the line tangent to these circles at \(A\) and \(B\),
respectively, so that \(M\) lies closer to \(AB\) than \(N\).
Let \(CD\) be the line parallel to \(AB\)
and passing through the point \(M\),
with \(C\) on \(G_1\) and \(D\) on \(G_2\).
Lines \(AC\) and \(BD\) meet at \(E\); lines \(AN\) and \(CD\) meet at \(P\);
lines \(BN\) and \(CD\) meet at \(Q\).
Show that \(EP = EQ\).

solutions.text:
First, we have \(\measuredangle EAB = \measuredangle ACM = \measuredangle BAM\)
and similarly \(\measuredangle EBA = \measuredangle BDM = \measuredangle ABM\).
Consequently, \(\overline{AB}\) bisects \(\angle EAM\) and \(\angle EBM\),
and hence \(\triangle EAB \cong \triangle MAB\).

[Diagram omitted from this imported TeX transcription.]

Now it is well-known that \(\overline{MN}\) bisects \(\overline{AB}\)
and since \(\overline{AB} \parallel \overline{PQ}\)
we deduce that \(M\) is the midpoint of \(\overline{PQ}\).
As \(\overline{AB}\) is the perpendicular bisector of \(\overline{EM}\),
it follows that \(EP = EQ\) as well.
